findings.what: _derive_samples positions the stencil at `col + px*cell_w` and `row + py*cell_h`. The cell origin is never multiplied by the cell size.
findings.why: Every cell except (0, 0) samples the wrong source pixels whenever cell_w or cell_h > 1. Example: pixel_size=2, px=0.25, col 1 samples x=1, which is inside cell 0; the correct x is 2. samples is wrong for any renderer that reads it. The tests only check samples[0, 0], so they cannot see this.
findings.fix: Use xi = floor((col + px) * cell_w) and yi = floor((row + py) * cell_h), clamped to [col*cell_w, (col+1)*cell_w - 1] so that px=1.0 cannot spill into the next cell. Add a test that checks a cell other than (0, 0), e.g. samples[1, 2].

findings.what: The sub-point pass dithers `np.repeat(cells, sy/sx)`, a nearest-neighbour upsample of the cell averages, not the step-5 image reduced to (rows·sy, cols·sx).
findings.why: S3 asks the pipeline to run the algorithm at sub-point resolution so that sub-points carry detail from inside the cell (braille/sextant bitmasks). With repeated cell averages, every point-wise algorithm puts the same index on all sub-points of a cell. Only error diffusion produces variation, and that variation is noise, not source detail. test_subindices_have_the_subgrid_shape_and_dtype even asserts `subindex == subindex[:, :, :1]`, which writes this defect into the test.
findings.fix: Build the sub-image by area-downscaling the padded step-5 work so each sub-point averages a (cell_w/sx × cell_h/sy) block. Use a fractional/box resample when the cell size is not divisible by the subgrid, or define it as at least one pixel per sub-point. Run the algorithm on that image. Replace the 'all sub-points equal' assertion with a test where a horizontal edge inside one cell gives different sub-indices.

findings.what: About 20 tests of frozen 1.0 behaviour were deleted from the existing suite rather than kept: output shape/dtype per pixel_size, uniform blocks, max_side reduce/keep/reject-zero, post-effect order, determinism, seed changes noise, brightness before dither, pre-effects before adjust, post-effects run last, algorithm params resolved/clamped, unknown param, bad shape, every resolve_palette test (custom, errors, >256, unknown source, builtin lazy import, extracted), custom palette drives render, and the pre_effects branch of the disabled-effect seed test. test_post_effects_run_after_upscale was also weakened to check a single block.
findings.why: The card's acceptance says 'la suite existante (1257) reste verte'. Removing regression coverage of frozen behaviour defeats G7 and the E6 guard. A green G2 means less once these tests are gone.
findings.fix: Restore every deleted test unchanged. The `test_registry` fixture can stay autouse. Add the new L2b tests next to the old ones rather than replacing them.

findings.what: Without sample_points(), the default stencil is a single centre point (k=1) whatever the renderer. The card asks for 'grille uniforme de k points'.
findings.why: k is a renderer property (§3: braille 8, sextant 6, quadrant 4, which is sx·sy in each case). A (2, 3) renderer with no sample_points() receives samples of shape (rows, cols, 1) instead of 6 points. This also changes the default samples from the cell-mean luma of L2 to the luma of one pixel.
findings.fix: Default to the uniform sx×sy grid of cell centres ((c+0.5)/sx, (r+0.5)/sy) with k = sx·sy. For subgrid (1, 1), keep the cell-mean luma, or document why one point is enough. Test that a subgrid (2, 3) stub without sample_points gets samples.shape[-1] == 6 at the expected positions.

findings.what: test_subpoint_coverage_is_monotone_at_the_subgrid_resolution sorts coverage by palette index and checks that it is non-decreasing.
findings.why: This only restates that the test palette is listed in ascending luminance. It passes for any subindex content, including all zeros or random values, so it cannot fail. The S3 requirement is that sub-point coverage is monotone along a source luminance gradient at sub-point resolution.
findings.fix: Render a horizontal luminance ramp whose width is a multiple of cols·sx through a point-wise algorithm. Flatten subindex back to (rows·sy, cols·sx) and assert that coverage is non-decreasing along x.

findings.what: The pixel parity check uses 1 image × 1 palette, with an image size divisible by pixel_size, and computes its expected value with the new prepare_image.
findings.why: The acceptance asks for 20 random images × 5 float palettes. The expected value comes from the code under test and not from the frozen 1.0 path, so a shared defect in _prepare/_to_cells would cancel out.
findings.fix: Parametrise over 20 seeded images with sizes not divisible by pixel_size, 5 float palettes and several pixel sizes. Compute the expected value independently: color.downscale → nearest_index → apply_palette → upscale_nearest on the raw source.

findings.what: _derive_samples has no type hints and no docstring. Docstrings were removed from about a dozen existing functions (_palette_for, _validate_order, _cell_geometry, _to_cells, _render_frame, _make_grid, _coverage_table, _apply_effects, _hex_*, _locked_colors, _palette_from_hex). The _as_image/_proxy/_pixel_size helpers were inlined into _prepare/_cell_geometry.
findings.why: This is a hygiene regression: it looks like the coder traded documentation for staying under the 400-line limit. _finish is now one function of about 60 lines.
findings.fix: Restore the docstrings. Move the sub-point pass and the grid build out of _finish into helpers (e.g. _subindex(...)), and split pipeline.py if the length limit requires it.

findings.what: The half-null check runs only inside _finish. prepare_image treats a half-null spec as continuous and returns the step-5 image without raising.
findings.why: The two entry points behave inconsistently for the same invalid spec.
findings.fix: Validate the continuous-mode pair once, in a helper called by both prepare_image and _finish.

regression: none observed for pixel output: pre-padding before color.downscale is equivalent, because downscale already edge-pads, and pixel geometry at aspect 1.0 is unchanged. The default grid.samples did change, from the cell-mean luma to the luma of one pixel; pixel does not read samples. Regression coverage was lost: about 20 frozen-behaviour tests were deleted.
renderer_invariants: Invariants 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 hold. render_frame is now shape-checked against invariant 1, and RenderStyle copies its options, which closes the hole in invariant 6. Invariant 3 is not tested in this diff; the pipeline itself does not mutate the grid or palette. The data the pipeline hands renderers is wrong: samples and subindex are miscomputed (see the two blockers).
tests_that_cannot_fail: test_subpoint_coverage_is_monotone_at_the_subgrid_resolution (only checks that the test palette is in ascending luminance order)
test_continuous_mode_matches_step5_to_post, first half (compares render with prepare_image; both run the same _prepare)
test_samples_follow_the_stencil_positions_into_the_source / test_default_stencil_is_a_single_centre_point (only check cell (0,0), where the missing col*cell_w factor has no effect)
test_subindices_have_the_subgrid_shape_and_dtype last assertion (asserts the defect: all sub-points equal)
notes: These parts conform to the card: the geometry rule (§5-6), the continuous-mode skip, render_frame shape guard, RenderStyle copy, spec renderer/renderer_style propagation, and the KeyError/ValueError paths. I found no abstraction leak (E8) and no host coupling (E9). The two blockers are maths errors in the step-10 data handed to renderers; they will hit braille, sextant and glyph_shape as soon as those renderers land. Out of scope here: from_json ignores renderer/renderer_style (presets.py), so presets lose the renderer on a round-trip. DEV-205 should track that before L3/L5.
